bandReport.notes: 20 items, 41-60, no gaps and no repeats. Item 41 opens at the top of p10-c1 and item 60 closes at the foot of p13-c2, so nothing spills past either band edge. COLUMN SPLIT — systematic, on all four pages: the detected gutter sits just RIGHT of the right column's number gutter, so every c1 crop carries the RIGHT column's item NUMBERS down its right edge (p10-c1 shows 43./44.; p11-c1 shows 48./49./50.; p12-c1 shows 54./55.; p13-c1 shows 58./59./60.) and each c2 crop is correspondingly MISSING its own item numbers, opening with a bare stray '.' glyph. No body text crossed the split and no option block was displaced; every right-column item number was recovered from the c1 edge AND independently confirmed against the whole-page pNN.png, and each c2 stem/option block was read only from c2. Q41 option (b) is printed 'International Panel of Climate Change' (not 'Intergovernmental') — transcribed verbatim as printed; do not 'correct' it. Q44 prints its subscripts with a raised-dot decimal, PM(2.5) set as 'PM' with subscript '2·5'; transcribed as \(\text{PM}_{2.5}\), which is the same value. Q47 prints 'not' in bold italic; kept as **not** because the emphasis carries the question. Q56's pairs are set as a genuine two-column grid under the headings 'Historical person' / 'Known as' and are transcribed as a pipe table. Pages 12 and 13 carry visible Hindi bleed-through from the reverse side of the sheet — cosmetic only, no English text obscured. Scan is ~150 DPI but every digit and option letter in this band was legible; nothing was guessed.
